[[File:Clethra arborea in the second week of October 1999 in Madeira..jpg|thumb|''Clethra arborea'']]

'''''Clethra arborea''''', commonly known as the '''lily-of-the-valley-tree''',<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |accessdate=2014-10-17 }}</ref> is a [[flowering plant]] in the genus ''[[Clethra]]''. It is found in [[Macaronesia]] where it is native to [[Madeira]], [[extinction|extinct]] in the [[Canary Islands]],<ref name=USDA>{{Citation
 | title =Histoire naturelle des îles Canaries (Philipp Barker Webb & Sabin Berthelot)
 | year =1836
 | publisher =Ministre de l'Instruction Publique
 | url =https://books.google.com/books?id=EyAuapBeAogC&q=Histoire+naturelle+des+%C3%AEles+Canaries++Par+Philip+Barker+Webb+clethra&pg=PA12
 }}</ref> and considered an introduced species in the [[Azores]].  In Madeira its natural habitat is [[laurisilva]] [[forest]].

==Description==
It is an [[evergreen]] narrowly upright [[shrub]] or small [[tree]], growing to about 6 m tall and 4 m wide. The [[leaf|foliage]] is dense and glossy, with the leaves up to 7–10 cm long. The [[flower]]s are small, white and [[fragrance|fragrant]], similar in appearance to those of [[lily of the valley]], hence the [[common name]]. (Lily of the valley is not closely related, being a [[monocotyledon]].) The flowers are grouped in terminal [[panicle]]s and bloom in early to mid summer.<ref name=CE>Cool Exotics.</ref>  The plant is toxic to humans; it contains [[Grayanotoxin|andromedotoxin]] which may cause [[diarrhea]] and even sudden [[death]].<ref name=TFD>The Free Dictionary.</ref>

==Cultivation==
The tree prefers moist, acidic and well-drained [[soil]]s, disliking alkaline soils. It is sensitive to [[frost]] and likely to die if the temperature falls below −3 °C. It is [[Plant propagation|propagated]] by [[seed]]s, [[Cutting (plant)|cuttings]] and [[Air layering|air-layering]].<ref name=CE/>
